claims.quote: There will people in America and its possessions by the lapse of another century.
claims.description: The population of the United States and its possessions will reach about five hundred million.
claims.stated_time: by the lapse of another century

claims.quote: Nicaragua will ask for admission to our Union after the completion of the great canal.
claims.description: Nicaragua will seek admission to the United States after a canal across Central America is finished.

claims.quote: Europe, seeking more territory to the south of us, will cause many of the South and Central American republics to be voted into the Union by their own people.
claims.description: Latin American republics will vote to join the United States under pressure from European expansion.

claims.quote: His increase of stature will result from better health, due to vast reforms in medicine, sanitation, food and athletics.
claims.description: Americans will grow one to two inches taller because of better medicine, sanitation, diet and exercise.

claims.quote: He will live fifty years instead of thirty-five as at present —for he will reside in the suburbs.
claims.description: Average life expectancy will rise from about thirty-five years to fifty because people will live in the suburbs.

claims.quote: The city house will practically be no more.
claims.description: Urban apartment and row housing will largely disappear in favor of suburban homes.

claims.quote: The trip from suburban home to office will require a few minutes only.
claims.description: Commuting from a suburban home to the office will take only a few minutes.

claims.quote: There will be No C, X or Q in our every-day alphabet.
claims.description: English will drop the letters C, X and Q from its alphabet as unnecessary.

claims.quote: Spelling by sound will have been adopted, first by the newspapers.
claims.description: English spelling will be reformed to follow pronunciation, starting with newspapers.

claims.quote: english will be a language of condensed words expressing condensed ideas, and will be more extensively spoken than any other.
claims.description: English will become the world's most widely spoken language, built on compressed vocabulary.

claims.quote: Hot or cold air will be turned on from spigots to regulate the temperature of a house as we now turn on hot or cold water from spigots to regulate the temperature of the bath.
claims.description: Houses will be heated and cooled by air piped in from valves, as water is now.

claims.quote: Central plants will supply this cool air and heat to city houses in the same way as now our gas or electricity is furnished.
claims.description: Central utility plants will deliver heating and cooling to city houses like gas or electric service.

claims.quote: Homes will have no chimneys, because no smoke will be created within their walls.
claims.description: Homes will be heated without fuel combustion, so they need no chimneys.

claims.quote: Mosquitoes, house-flies and roaches will have been practically exterminated.
claims.description: Mosquitoes, house flies and cockroaches will be nearly wiped out.

claims.quote: Boards of health will have cael all mosquito haunts and breeding-grounds, drained all stagnant pools, filled in all swamp-lands, and chemically treated all still-water streams.
claims.description: Public health boards will drain swamps and chemically treat standing water to eliminate disease insects.

claims.quote: The extermination of the horse and its stable will reduce the house-fly.
claims.description: Removing horses and their stables will reduce the house fly population.

claims.quote: They will purchase materials in tremendous wholesale quantities and sell the cooked foods at a price much lower than the cost of individual cooking.
claims.description: Central kitchens will sell prepared meals more cheaply than households can cook them.

claims.quote: Food will be served hot or cold to private houses in pneumatic tubes or automobile wagons.
claims.description: Prepared meals will be delivered to homes by pneumatic tube or automobile van.

claims.quote: Such wholesale cookery will be done in clectric laboratories rather than in kitchens.
claims.description: Bulk food preparation will move from home kitchens into electric central facilities.

claims.quote: Having one's own cook and purchasing one's own food will be an extravagance.
claims.description: Keeping a private cook and buying one's own ingredients will be seen as a luxury.

claims.quote: Liquid-air refrigerators will keep great quantities of food fresh for long intervals.
claims.description: Liquid-air refrigerators will preserve large amounts of food for long periods.

claims.quote: Storekeepers who expose food to air breathed out by patrons or to the atmosphere of the busy streets will be arrested with those who sell stale or adulterated produce.
claims.description: Food sanitation laws will make it a crime to sell food exposed to breath or street air.

claims.quote: The earth’s hard coal will last until the year 2050 or 2100; its soft-coal mines until 2200 or 2300.
claims.description: Hard coal reserves will run out around 2050 to 2100 and soft coal around 2200 to 2300.

claims.quote: Man will have found electricity manufactured by water-power to be much cheaper.
claims.description: Hydroelectric power will become much cheaper than coal-generated electricity.

claims.quote: Every river or creek with any suitable fall will be equipped with water-motors, turning dynamos, making electricity.
claims.description: Hydroelectric turbines will be installed on every usable stream to generate electricity.

claims.quote: Along the seacoast will be numerous reservoirs continually filled by waves and tides washing in.
claims.description: Coastal reservoirs filled by waves and tides will drive water wheels to generate power.

claims.quote: All hurry traffic will be below or high above ground when brought within city limits.
claims.description: Fast urban transport will run in tunnels or on elevated trestles rather than at street level.

claims.quote: Cities, therefore, will be free from all noises.
claims.description: Cities will be quiet because fast traffic is moved underground or overhead.

claims.quote: These underground or overhead streets will teem with capacious automobile passenger coaches and freight wagons, with cushioned wheels.
claims.description: Underground and elevated urban roadways will carry large automobile passenger coaches and freight vehicles.

claims.quote: If there be a battle in China a hundred years hence snapshots of its most striking events will be published in the newspapers an hour later.
claims.description: Photographs of distant events will be transmitted by telegraph and printed within an hour.

claims.quote: Photographs will reproduce all of Nature’s colors.
claims.description: Photographs will capture and reproduce the full range of natural colors.

claims.quote: Trains will run two miles a minute, normally ; express trains one hundred and fifty miles an hour.
claims.description: Trains will routinely travel at about 120 mph and express trains at 150 mph.

claims.quote: To go from New York to San Francisco will take a day and a night by fast express.
claims.description: A coast-to-coast rail trip will take about 36 hours by fast express.

claims.quote: There will be cigar-shaped electric locomotives hauling long trains of cars.
claims.description: Trains will be pulled by streamlined electric locomotives.

claims.quote: Cars will, like houses, be artificially cooled.
claims.description: Passenger railway cars will have mechanical air conditioning.

claims.quote: Along the railroads there will be no smoke, no cinders, because coal will neither be carried nor burned.
claims.description: Railroads will run without coal, so there will be no smoke or cinders.

claims.quote: A onepound motor in one of these vehicles will do the work of a vair Of horses or more.
claims.description: A one-pound motor will do the work of a team of horses in a farm vehicle.

claims.quote: Automobiles will have been substituted for every horse vehicle now known.
claims.description: Motor vehicles will replace every horse-drawn vehicle in use.

claims.quote: Exercise will be compulsory in the schools.
claims.description: Physical exercise will be required in all schools.

claims.quote: A manor woman unable to walk ten miles at a stretch will be regarded as a weakling.
claims.description: Being unable to walk ten miles at a stretch will be considered a sign of weakness.

claims.quote: Fast electric ships, crossing the ocean at more than a mile a minute, will go from New York to Liverpool in two days.
claims.description: Electric ships will cross the Atlantic at over sixty miles an hour, taking two days from New York to Liverpool.

claims.quote: Upon their under sides will be apertures expelling jets of air.
claims.description: Ship hulls will eject air jets from their undersides to form an air film that lowers water friction.

claims.quote: Propellers turned by electricity will screw themselves through both the water beneath and the air above.
claims.description: Electrically driven propellers will move a craft through both water and air.

claims.quote: There will be Air-Ships, but they will not successfully compete with surface cars and water vessels for passenger or freight traffic.
claims.description: Airships will exist but will not win commercial passenger or freight traffic from trains and ships.

claims.quote: They will be maintained as deadly warvessels by all military nations.
claims.description: Airships will be kept as military weapons by all major armed forces.

claims.quote: Giant guns will shoot twenty-five miles or more, and will hurl anywhere within such a radius shells exploding and destroying whole cities.
claims.description: Giant artillery will fire shells twenty-five miles or farther to destroy whole cities.

claims.quote: Such guns will be aimed by aid of compasses When used on land or sea, and telescopes when directed from great heights.
claims.description: Long-range guns will be aimed using compasses at sea and telescopes from high altitudes.

claims.quote: Fleets of air-ships, hiding themselves with dense, smoky mists, thrown off by themselves as they move, will float over cities, fortifications, camps or fleets.
claims.description: Airship fleets will hide in self-generated smoke screens while attacking cities and armies from above.

claims.quote: These aérial war-ships will necessitate bomb-proof forts, protected by great steel plates over their tops as well as at their sides.
claims.description: Aerial warships will force fortifications to be armored on top as well as on the sides.

claims.quote: Huge forts on wheels will dash across open spaces at the speed of express trains of to-day.
claims.description: Armored mobile fortresses on wheels will move across battlefields at express train speeds.

claims.quote: Great automobile plows will dig deep intrenchments as fast as soldiers can occupy them.
claims.description: Motorized plows will dig trenches as fast as troops can occupy them.

claims.quote: Rifles will use silent cartridges.
claims.description: Rifles will fire silenced ammunition.

claims.quote: Submarine boats submerged for days will be capable of wiping a whole navy off the tace of the deep.
claims.description: Submarines that stay submerged for days will be able to sink an entire navy.

claims.quote: Balloons and flying machines will carry telescopes of one-hundred-mile vision with camera attachments, photographing an enemy within that radius.
claims.description: Balloons and aircraft will carry long-range cameras that photograph enemy positions a hundred miles away.

claims.quote: Rats and mice will have been exterminated.
claims.description: Rats and mice will be wiped out.

claims.quote: Food animals will be bred to expend practically all of their life energy in producing meat, milk, wool and other by-products.
claims.description: Livestock will be bred to put nearly all their energy into meat, milk and wool, with horns and bones selected away.

claims.quote: Persons and things of all kinds will be brought within focus of cameras connected electrically with screens at opposite ends of circuits, thousands of miles at a span.
claims.description: Live video of people and events will be transmitted electrically over thousands of miles to distant screens.

claims.quote: American audiences in their theatres will view upon huge curtains before them the coronations of kings in Europe or the progress of battles in the Orient.
claims.description: Theater audiences will watch live images of distant events, such as coronations and battles, on large screens.

claims.quote: Thus the guns of a distant battle will be heard to boom when seen to blaze, and thus the lips of a remote actor or singer will be heard to utter words or music when seen to move.
claims.description: Distant video will be paired with synchronized sound so remote speech and gunfire are heard in step with the images.

claims.quote: Wireless telephone and telegraph circuits will span the world.
claims.description: Wireless telephone and telegraph links will connect every part of the globe.

claims.quote: A husband in the middle of the Atlantic will be able to converse with his wife sitting in her boudoir in Chicago.
claims.description: A passenger at sea will be able to hold a wireless voice call with someone on land thousands of miles away.

claims.quote: By an automatic signal they will connect with any circuit in their locality without the intervention of a
claims.description: Telephone calls will be connected automatically by signal, with no switchboard operator.

claims.quote: Grand Opera will be Telephoned to private homes, and will sound as harmonious as though enjoyed from a theatre box.
claims.description: Live opera will be carried by telephone into private homes with near-concert quality.

claims.quote: Automatic instruments reproducing original airs exactly will bring the best music to the families of the untalented.
claims.description: Mechanical instruments will reproduce recorded music exactly for households.

claims.quote: Great musicians gathered in one inclosure in New York will, by manipulating electric keys, produce at the same time music from instruments arranged in theatres or halls in San Francisco or New Orleans, for instance.
claims.description: Musicians in one city will play electrically linked instruments in distant halls at the same time, creating long-distance concerts.

claims.quote: The piano will be capable of changing its tone from cheerful to sad.
claims.description: Pianos will be able to change their tone from cheerful to sad.

claims.quote: A university education will be free to every man and woman.
claims.description: University education will be tuition-free for all adults.

claims.quote: Medical inspectors regularly visiting the public schools will furnish poor children free eyeglasses, free dentistry and free medical attention of every kind.
claims.description: School medical inspectors will provide free eyeglasses, dental care and medical treatment to poor children.

claims.quote: Pneumatic tubes, instead of store wagons, will deliver packages and bundles.
claims.description: Pneumatic tubes will deliver store purchases to homes in place of delivery wagons.

claims.quote: These tubes will collect, deliver and transport mail over certain distances, perhaps for hundreds of miles.
claims.description: Pneumatic tube networks will carry mail over hundreds of miles.

claims.quote: In cold weather he will place heat-conducting electric wires under the soil of his garden and thus warm his growing plants.
claims.description: Farmers will heat garden soil with buried electric wires to grow plants in cold weather.

claims.quote: At night his vegetables will be bathed in powerful electric light, serving, like sunlight, to hasten their growth.
claims.description: Crops will be grown under artificial electric light at night to speed growth.

claims.quote: Electric currents applied to the soil will make valuable plants grow larger and faster, and will kill troublesome weeds.
claims.description: Electric current applied to soil will accelerate crop growth and kill weeds.

claims.quote: Fast-tlying refrigerators on land and sea will bring delicious fruits from the tropics and southern temperate zone within a few days.
claims.description: Fast refrigerated transport by rail and ship will bring tropical and southern fruit to northern markets within days.

claims.quote: Scientists will have discovered how to raise here many fruits now confined to much hotter or colder climates.
claims.description: Scientists will develop methods to grow tropical and subarctic fruits in temperate regions.

claims.quote: Strawberries as Large as Apples will be eaten by our great-great-grandchildren for their Christmas dinners a hundred years hence.
claims.description: Strawberries will grow as large as apples.

claims.quote: Melons, cherries, grapes, plums, apples, pears, peaches and all berries will be seedless.
claims.description: Most fruits will be bred to be seedless.

claims.quote: The milkweed will have been developed into a rubber plant.
claims.description: Milkweed will be bred into a commercial rubber crop.

claims.quote: Plants will be made proof against disease microbes just as readily as man is to-day against smallpox.
claims.description: Crop plants will be made resistant to disease microbes through engineering.

claims.quote: The soil will be kept enriched by plants which take their nutrition from the air and give fertility to the earth.
claims.description: Plants will be bred to draw nutrients from the air and enrich the soil, as nitrogen-fixing crops do.

claims.quote: There will be black, blue and green roses.
claims.description: Roses will be bred in black, blue and green colors.

claims.quote: It will be possible to grow any flower in any color and to transfer the perfume of a scented flower to another which is odorless.
claims.description: Flowers will be grown in any color and scent will be transferred between species.

claims.quote: Few Drugs will be Swallowed or taken into the stomach unless needed for the direct treatment of that organ itself.
claims.description: Most drugs will be delivered by routes other than swallowing, so they reach only the organ they treat.

claims.quote: Drugs needed by the lungs, for instance, will be applied directly to those organs through the skin and flesh.
claims.description: Drugs will be delivered through the skin directly to organs such as the lungs.

claims.quote: They will be carried with the electric current applied without pain to the outside skin of the body.
claims.description: Drugs will be carried into the body by an electric current applied painlessly to the skin.

claims.quote: Microscopes will lay bare the vital organs, through the living flesh, of men and animals.
claims.description: Imaging devices will reveal living organs inside the body without surgery.

claims.quote: The living body will to all medical purposes be transparent.
claims.description: The living body will be effectively transparent to doctors, with internal organs visible through the flesh.

claims.quote: Not only will it be possible for a physician to actually see a living, throbbing heart inside the chest, but he will be able to magnify and photograph any part of it.
claims.description: Doctors will watch a living heart beating inside the chest and photograph any part of it.
